newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent rallies to highs from post-NYMEX dip.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent rallies to highs from post-NYMEX dip.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures were trading at session highs on Monday after recovering from a choppy, NYMEX-inspired retreat, trader said.
April Brent was up nine cents at $19.95 a barrel at 1609 GMT, after slumping to $19.73 twice in the 15 minutes following NYMEX's opening and a morning dip to $19.65.
March gas oil was down $1.25 at $167.75 a tonne, 75 cents off the high.
Traders said the fall on IPE Brent was triggered by repeated attempts to drive April WTI below $21, a movement aided by lacklustre early performances in U.S. gasoline and heating oil.
But Brent rallied as NYMEX and U.S. products shrugged off the selling. WTI climbed to $21.20 a barrel, five cents off the high.
Brent intermonths spreads were steady at around +17 cents for April/May and +10 cents for May/June.
Traders saw support for Brent at $19.60, and failing that the $19.15-$19.16 area, with resistance at Friday's high of $20.07 and then $20.62.
Traders said March gas oil was also suffering a lull as the contract neared its expiry on Wednesday.
Traders saw resistance at around $169-$170 a tonne and $172 above that. Support was seen at $165-$165.50, and if that does not hold, anything down to $160.

Traders said Brent continued to reflect fundamental weakness in the period between seasonal gasoline and heating oil demand peaks. But front month Brent nevertheless appeared to be successfully building a short-term trading range of around $19.60/90.
